hypothesis: Predict each candidate public observation's expected reduction in uncertainty using experience from past public-coordinate anomalies, then choose the two most informative unseen sensors at each episode, rather than selecting from predefined schedule rules.

mechanism.train_labels: Only actual public-coordinate calibrated anomalies in F9 previously consumed training traces
mechanism.learned_signal: smoothed Bernoulli posterior uncertainty reduction p*(1-p)
mechanism.training_feature_context: episode, previous observed anomaly, offset relative to publicly inferred rotation

evaluation.primary: physical matching mismatch episodes across 96 previously used development cases (engineering only)
secondary: publicly driven changes to sensor addresses
evaluation.negative: No gain against the best fixed comparator, or choosing a constant address set under all prior public histories, is a negative for adaptive information-value gains
